title: Hotel Check-in in China
metaDescription: Practical China hotel check-in guidance for foreign visitors, including passports, registration, booking confirmation, and payment backups.

sections.heading: Getting Started
sections.content: Hotels should not refuse an overseas guest merely by claiming they lack a special foreign-guest qualification. Your physical passport is normally required so the property can verify your identity and complete accommodation registration. Before a non-refundable booking, ask the exact property to confirm passport check-in, reception hours, and late-arrival arrangements in writing.

sections.heading: Key Tips
sections.content: Bring the physical passport used for the reservation and enter every guest name exactly as it appears in that document. Keep the hotel name, address, and phone number in Chinese. Some front desks may be unfamiliar with foreign-passport registration, so save the booking platform confirmation and contact NIA 12367 if a registration problem cannot be resolved.

sections.heading: What to Remember
sections.content: Deposits and accepted payment methods vary by property. Confirm the amount and refund method before paying, and keep a card or RMB cash backup. If staff incorrectly cite a missing foreign-related qualification, calmly ask them to check the passport-registration process, contact the booking platform, or call 12367 for guidance.

keyTakeaways: Confirm passport registration and reception hours directly before a restrictive booking
Bring the physical passport used for the reservation
Carry cash or set up Alipay/WeChat Pay as backup payment options
